answer: Sybil resistance for AI agents hinges on a verifiable, costly unique identifier. Each agent must cryptographically attest to a specialized hardware module, akin to an 'onyx' security chip. This creates an economic barrier: fabricating enough unique modules to launch a Sybil attack and turn the tide of network integrity becomes prohibitively expensive. An attacker's resource expenditure would resemble forging rare comet signatures, making large-scale impersonation unviable.
